reigns.note: Eponymous son of Aetolus by Pronoe; with his brother Pleuron he gave his name to the Aetolian city that heads the house.
Homeric Portheus, son of Agenor by Epicaste daughter of Calydon; father of Oeneus, Agrius, and Melas, whose sons dwelt in Pleuron and steep Calydon.
Reigning over Calydon, first to receive the vine from Dionysus; father of Meleager, who slighted Artemis and loosed the boar.
Son of Oeneus to whom commands had been given that he should bear full sway among the Aetolians; dead before the Trojan muster, after the Curetes war and the brand.
Brother of Oeneus; his sons wrested Calydon from the aged king and gave the kingdom to their father until Diomedes restored the house.
Husband of Gorge; Diomedes gave him the kingdom when Oeneus was too old to rule, and his son Thoas later led the Aetolians.
Son of Andraemon and Gorge; lord of Pleuron and steep Calydon when the Aetolians sailed to Troy after Oeneus' house fell.
